gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, in bag mode, the ANTHBOT N8 needs about 15–22 hours of mowing to cover its rated 0.37 acre once. That comes from two named measurements: Notebookcheck got about 100 m² per hour and PCWorld about 740 sq ft per hour. It works out to roughly 7–13 battery charges per full cut.
standout_why: I read four reviews: PCWorld (cited) and Notebookcheck (a result but not cited) on the N8, T3 (cited) on the N8, and T3 and Notebookcheck on the YUKA. I also read the uncited top results from NeoIntell and MowerBotLab. PCWorld gives the raw rate (1,200 sq ft in 97 min) and Notebookcheck gives just under 200 m² per roughly 2-hour charge. Neither turns that into hours or charges for the 0.37-acre rating, and ChatGPT repeated the rating without that caveat. T3's N8 review has no measurements at all: no dB, no time, no coverage. NeoIntell and MowerBotLab have no measurements, and NeoIntell names only the YUKA as a mower that collects clippings. The raw figures are already in the results, so only the conversion and the side-by-side comparison are new.
decides: This confirms the N8 as the pick for real bagging. It is the only built-in collector, and both PCWorld and Notebookcheck saw it empty itself reliably. The size advice changes, though. Measured at about 740–1,075 sq ft per hour in bag mode, a 5,000 sq ft lawn takes about 5–7 hours of mowing per cut, and the full 0.37-acre rating takes all day across many charges. Two reviewers measured it at about 68–70 dB at 1 m, against Anthbot's own 58 dB claim for mowing and mulching. Notebookcheck measured the YUKA 1000 with its sweeper at about the same noise (about 70 dB). The YUKA's sweeper also drops its slope limit from 45% to 18%, so the YUKA is no quieter and handles slopes worse when collecting.

findings.label: Noise while collecting (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: This robotic lawn mower makes sense in autumn too: Anthbot N8 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Measured by Marcus Schwarten, published 2026-10-03 and updated 2026-10-09. He calls it almost as loud as a conventional mower. A quieter mode with lower blade speed is available.

findings.label: Noise in collection mode (PCWorld)
findings.value: just under 68 dB at 3.28 ft (1 m)
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: Measured by Michael Rupp, published 2026-10-01, firmware 0.3.90.

findings.label: Maker's noise claim (for contrast)
findings.value: 58 dB (mow/mulch); 'Standard mode noise ≤ 60dB'; no figure given for collecting
findings.note: The two measured collection-mode figures (68–70 dB) are about 10–12 dB above the maker's mow/mulch figure. The same page shows the price at $1,359.00, down from $1,699.00, on 2026-11-17.

findings.label: Coverage rate with bag (PCWorld)
findings.value: 1,200 sq ft in 97 min ≈ 740 sq ft/h; 960 sq ft used about 80% of a charge
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: My arithmetic: 960 ÷ 0.8 ≈ 1,200 sq ft per full charge. The rated 0.37 acre is about 16,100 sq ft, so 16,100 ÷ 740 ≈ 22 h of mowing, or about 13 charges. PCWorld measured charging at 80 min.

findings.label: Runtime and area per charge (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about 2 h runtime covering just under 200 m² (≈100 m²/h, ≈1,075 sq ft/h); returned with just under 15% left; recharge about 1.5 h, a good 200 Wh from the wall
findings.source_title: This robotic lawn mower makes sense in autumn too: Anthbot N8 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: My arithmetic: the rated 1,500 m² ÷ 100 m²/h ≈ 15 h of mowing, or about 7.5 charges. Adding about 1.5 h of charging per cycle gives roughly 26 h of elapsed time per full cut. Standby draw at the station was over 10 W.

findings.label: Auto-empty interval (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about every 100 minutes, plus once at the end of each session; the interval can't be changed
findings.source_title: This robotic lawn mower makes sense in autumn too: Anthbot N8 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Observed in testing, not measured as a fill level. PCWorld separately reports that auto-dumping never failed during its test.

findings.label: Uncut edge strip (PCWorld)
findings.source_title: Anthbot N8 review: Leaf cleanup is where this mower stands out | PCWorld
findings.note: Depends on distance to walls and obstacles. Three edge passes narrowed the strip but didn't remove it.

findings.label: Noise with sweeper fitted (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: This wireless robotic lawnmower can also collect leaves: Mammotion Yuka 2025 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Measured by Marcus Schwarten, published 2025-04-28. The review doesn't state the measuring distance. Without the sweeper the noise is only called unremarkable, with no number.

findings.label: Slope limit with and without sweeper (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 45% (24°) on the test ramp without the sweeper; 18% (10°) with it
findings.source_title: This wireless robotic lawnmower can also collect leaves: Mammotion Yuka 2025 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: The 45% figure was confirmed on the ramp. The review doesn't say whether the 18% sweeper figure was tested or quoted from the spec.

findings.label: Area per charge, energy and edge (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: about 230 m² per charge in just under 2 h (no sweeper, standard settings); 15→100% recharge about 2 h, about 145 Wh at up to 85 W; standby about 10 W; uncut edge at least 10 cm; needs passages of at least 100 cm
findings.source_title: This wireless robotic lawnmower can also collect leaves: Mammotion Yuka 2025 review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: This was measured without the sweeper, so it doesn't compare directly with the N8's bag-mode rate. The reviewer estimates about 13 kWh a month for 500 m² mowed three times a week.

findings.label: Collection result (T3)
findings.value: 'the vast majority of grass clippings'; about 90% of leaves (reviewer says leaves weren't fully tested); 22 L catcher; slope 45% without the catcher, 18% with it
findings.source_title: Mammotion YUKA 1500 3D Vision Robot Lawn Sweeping Mower review | T3
findings.note: Derek Adams, 2024-08-09, after two weeks of use. The collection result is an estimate, not a lab measurement.
